raw_text: ABSTRACT: Polycyclic polyprenylated acylphloroglucinols (PPAPs) combine compelling structural complexity with efective biological activity. The total synthesis of Hyperfirin is reported as one linear sequence. Key to this novel modular strategy is to access the bicyclo[3.3.1]nonane-2,4,9-trione framework via transannular acylation of a decorated eight-membered ring, followed by late stage bridgehead substitution. The described route adds flexibility to PPAP construction and broadens the scope of eight-membered

raw_text: P <sup>olycyclic</sup> <sup>polyprenylated</sup> <sup>acylphloroglucinols</sup> <sup>(PPAPs)</sup> <sup>are</sup> structually complex natural products found in plants of the genera Hypericum and Garcinia. Their complexity results from a densely substituted and highly oxygenated core structure. To date, more than a thousand natural PPAPs have been identified, the majority of which feature a bicyclo[3.3.1]- nonane-2,4,9-trione skeleton. raw_text: A 5.5:1 mixture of ketones 9a and 9b was synthesized via a slightly optimized literature procedure.<sup>24</sup> Conjugate addition with Me CuLi·LiCN was highly efective, right from the outset. The respective methylated ketones from 9a and 9b were obtained as separable regioisomers in quantitative yield following addition to the organocopper reagent and standard aqueous workup. Encouraged by these promising results, we examined the trapping of intermediate enolates 10a and 10b with 2-(trimethylsilyl)ethyl (TSE) cyanoformate (Scheme 2).

raw_text: Initial attempts resulted in the formation of the desired esters 11a and 11b alongside diesters 12a and 12b and nonreacted 10a and 10b. This can be explained via a competitive reaction between the initial enolate and the trapping agent or with the already formed ester. This subsequently gives rise to the formation of a new enolate that then reacts with the trapping agent. Best results were obtained by reducing the amount of cyanoformate to an absolute minimum and adding it neat in a single rapid shot. With 71% of sole 11a in hand, we focused on the regeneration of the double bond. Slow addition of PhSeCl at −100 °C should ensure the syn-conformation of the selenide and the proton at the tertiary center. Direct oxidation of the crude product with mCPBA furnished double activated Michael acceptor 13 in a 68% overall yield. The second conjugate addition yielded a 3:1 mixture of two separable diastereomers in 97% yield. Examination of the relative configuration by NOESY experiments proved ambiguous. Consequently, enol ether formation was attempted with both isomers separately, aiming to clarify the relative configuration at a later stage.

raw_text: We planned to perform enol ether formation via the respective dimethyl acetal and subsequent treatment with LDA under kinetic conditions.<sup>25</sup> Instead of acetal formation, both diastereomers were converted directly into their respective enol ethers in the presence of (±)-CSA and HC(OMe) in methanol. This can be rationalized through conjugative efects and steric hindrance. It should be noted that longer reaction times diminished the yield drastically. This may be caused by cleavage of the trimethysilylethyl ester and subsequent decomposition. To our delight, the relative configuration of 15 could be elucidated by X-ray crystallography at this point. With the configuration cleared, we sought to convert the undesired 14a to 14b via thermodynamic equilibration. Each cycle resulted in 65% of the desired diastereomer 14b based on the recovered amount of 14a.

raw_text: In light of our previous work<sup>26</sup> we turned to the construction of the bicyclic core. Treatment of 15 with 4 equiv of TBAF yielded the required carboxylic acid 16 in nearquantitative yield. To our surprise, our original transannular acylation protocol yielded a diverse array of compounds, none of which could be definitively identified. Comparison with our model systems suggested that either the enol ether moiety or the homoprenyl substituent underwent side reactions in the presence of trifluoroacetic acid or intermediate carbocation 18.

After the formation of mixed anhydride 17, the one-carbon bridge is formed selectively, with its configuration being determined by the orientation of the initial carboxylic acid 16. The intermediate ionic species 18 is then attacked by trifluoroacetate from the exo or endo face, leading to 19 as a mixture of only two diastereomers. Alternatively, the addition of trifluoroacetate to the vinylogous position results in 20 after hydrolysis. We did not try to further improve the diastereomeric ratio, as the isomeric mixture would be oxidized in the next step. Although we ultimately obtained 19 at this point, we faced severe problems with the reproducibility. It was found that NEt reacted with TFAA at a rate comparable to that of the substrate.<sup>27</sup> After screening for a suitable base we found, inspired by work from Shibasaki,<sup>2</sup> that 2,6-di-tert-butyl-4- methylpyridine efectively resolved our problem, allowing us to obtain 19 with a 70% overall yield.

raw_text: In summary, we successfully synthesized Hyperfirin (1) in a single 13-step sequence and 2.1% total yield from the literature known ketone 9. This route introduces a novel C-5−C-9 bond formation and enhanced flexibility to PPAP chemistry, while also providing valuable insights into eight-ring chemistry. It is our intention to exploit this strategy, especially in course to alter the C-5 and C-8 substitution pattern and synthesize a greater number of PPAPs.
